title: High-Resolution 3-Tesla MRI Examinations in Patients with Diseases of the Tooth, Periodontium, and Surrounding Tissues
summary:
Imaging of the teeth and adjacent structures has been established as a routine clinical diagnostic procedure in our department for several years and can effectively supplement—and possibly replace—X-ray examinations. We would like to further develop this method by comparing measurements taken from patients with diseases affecting their teeth and adjacent structures to those of healthy control subjects like you, and by scientifically evaluating the results. The goal of the study is to improve the diagnostic classification of damage to the teeth and their surrounding structures and to detect such damage at an earlier stage.
As part of the study, an MRI scan will be performed prior to the planned dental treatment. MRI is used to produce images of the body without X-rays. This imaging method has been routinely used worldwide for over 30 years. To date, no temporary or even permanent damage caused by MRI has been detected. The MRI scan will take between 40 and 70 minutes. In addition, a second MRI scan may be necessary for certain aspects of the study.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-    Age ≥ 18 years
-    Male and female patients with one of the following conditions:
1.    Periodontitis
2.    Chronic apical periodontitis—apical granuloma/cyst
3.    Unclear osteolytic/cystic space-occupying or neoplastic process in the jaw region
4.    Condition following dental trauma
5.    Condition following autologous tooth transplantation
6.    Condition following a revascularization attempt on a tooth with pulp necrosis
7.    Condition following pulpotomy
8.    Peri-endodontic lesions
9.    Osteomyelitis
-    Subjects with healthy teeth, aged 18 to 85 years, who will receive contrast medium
-    Signed informed consent form
Exclusion criteria:
-    Contraindications for an MRI scan (e.g., pacemaker, metal objects in a dangerous location [eye], cochlear implant, claustrophobia, etc.),
-    Contraindications for the administration of MR contrast agents (e.g., kidney disease, allergic reactions, etc.)
-    Pregnancy and breastfeeding
-    Acute or chronic kidney disease associated with impaired kidney function
